title: New Norwegian online newspaper has strong ties to party with link to Russia
content:
The online media describes itself as independent, but the man behind it is a member of the FOR party, NORDIS partner Faktisk.no reports. 

Towards the end of May, a Facebook post published by Fred og Rettferdighet (FOR) leader Marielle Leraand appeared. In it, she said that a new online newspaper called “Perspektiv” had been launched in Norway and that she was impressed by the articles she had read.

Vladimir Fedorov is behind the website, and confirms that he considers himself a member of the FOR party. According to Fedorov, it is coincidental that several people on the website’s editorial team are party members.

“They are simply people who share the same views, but it has nothing to do with the party. It just means that we are moving in the same direction as them,” says Fedorov.

FOR became known to the Norwegian public ahead of the 2025 parliamentary election, when it ran an advertising campaign against Norway providing financial support for Ukraine’s defence against Russia. Norwegian billionaire Atle Berge, who has business interests in Russia, confirmed that he supported the party financially.

title: Sweden’s election aftermath: How misinformation shaped the campaign
content:
NORDIS and its Swedish partners, Källkritikbyrån and the Fojo Media Institute, look back at an election marked by misinformation, from claims of election interference and voter fraud to AI-generated content. 

The Swedish elections are over, but the aftermath looks set to be dramatic as complex negotiations loom over the formation of a new Swedish government, following allegations of electoral fraud against several politicians.

Rumours of electoral fraud also played a role during the campaign. But looking back, can the election be described as one marked by misinformation?

NORDIS spoke to its Swedish partners at the fact-checking organisation Källkritikbyrån and the Fojo Media Institute at Linnaeus University about the role of misinformation in Sweden’s elections.
